overview: Super Retail Group is one of Australia and New Zealand's largest specialty retailers, operating four banners: Supercheap Auto (automotive parts and accessories), rebel (sporting goods and apparel), BCF (Boating Camping Fishing/outdoor leisure), and Macpac (technical outdoor apparel and equipment). The Group runs 797 stores across three countries (Australia, New Zealand and a small China sourcing/support presence) and generated $4.2 billion of sales in FY26, with management estimating its brands capture only around 10% of a combined $65 billion total addressable market in auto, sport and outdoor categories. The business is highly cash-generative and has pivoted from a five-year period of margin consolidation (FY20-FY26) into a newly announced five-year growth and transformation strategy launched in June 2026.

business_model.summary: Super Retail Group is a multi-banner specialty retailer that monetizes a large, high-frequency customer base through a portfolio approach: four differentiated banners share back-office scale (supply chain, distribution centres, systems, sourcing) while each targets a distinct category (auto, sport, outdoor/leisure, technical outdoor apparel). A key differentiator is the Group's loyalty/Club program infrastructure, which drives ~86% of Group retail sales through active club members and generates first-party data used for personalisation, promotions and CRM. Revenue is transactional (retail sales of goods, plus fitment/installation services at Supercheap Auto) rather than subscription-based, though loyalty membership fosters repeat-purchase behavior akin to recurring engagement.
business_model.customer_type: B2C mass-market and enthusiast consumers across auto, sport, outdoor and leisure categories, skewing toward Australian and New Zealand households; some B2B/trade sales through Supercheap Auto commercial fitment and rebel trade partnerships
business_model.geographic_mix: Australia (majority of sales and stores), New Zealand (meaningful presence in Supercheap Auto and Macpac, Macpac's home market), small China-based team supporting sourcing/supply chain
business_model.channel_mix: 87% in-store, 13% online ($552m in FY26, +5.3% YoY); of online sales, 47.5% is Click & Collect, meaning ~93% of all sales are ultimately completed/collected in-store
business_model.loyalty_program: 13.1 million active Club members (+4.8% YoY) representing 86% of Group retail sales; each banner runs its own program (Supercheap Auto 'Spend & Get' relaunched July 2025, rebel Active, BCF and Macpac club programs); loyalty data underpins personalisation and CRM and is a core plank of the new five-year strategy

main_competitors: Repco (Bapcor) and Autobarn/Autopro (independent auto parts networks) in automotive
JB Hi-Fi, Amazon Australia, Kogan.com, Catch and pure-play online retailers across general merchandise/leisure categories
Anaconda (Wesfarmers/Adventure Brands) and Kathmandu (KMD Brands) in outdoor/camping
Sporting goods independents, department stores (Big W, Kmart, Target) and direct-to-consumer brand websites (Nike, adidas) in sporting goods
Bunnings-adjacent hardware/outdoor overlap for camping and 4WD accessories
Trade partners increasingly selling direct-to-consumer, bypassing retail intermediaries
competitive_position.market_position: Category leader in Australian/NZ specialty auto parts (Supercheap Auto) and sporting goods (rebel); leading position in boating/camping/fishing (BCF) and a strong outdoor apparel niche via Macpac in NZ/Australia. Company estimates its four brands capture only ~10% of a $65bn combined addressable market, implying substantial white space but also fragmented, intensifying competition.

moat_factors.description: 13.1 million active members and 86% of sales tied to loyalty programs give SUL a first-party data advantage for personalisation, inventory and promotional targeting versus smaller independents; still a work in progress as a genuine switching-cost moat

Four banners across different categories smooth some cyclicality (e.g., BCF weak while Supercheap Auto/rebel solid in FY26) and allow shared supply chain/DC infrastructure (new Truganina DC services SCA, rebel and BCF)

Supercheap Auto has 91% brand awareness in Australia/93% in NZ; rebel and BCF are similarly the largest dedicated specialty retailers in their categories, giving negotiating leverage with suppliers/trade partners

797 stores plus Click & Collect infrastructure support fast fulfilment versus pure online players, though this is a defensive rather than differentiating advantage given e-commerce penetration is still only 13%

moat_factors.factor: Cost/scale advantage from supply chain investment
moat_factors.description: New Truganina distribution centre and Ignite transformation program targeted to unlock a 'sustainable cost advantage' but these are unproven, multi-year investments rather than a realized moat today

weaknesses: Discretionary retail categories are directly exposed to consumer confidence, fuel prices and interest rates; FY26 saw a marked slowdown from a Middle East-driven fuel price crisis
Online penetration (13%) lags pure-play and category-adjacent competitors, leaving exposure to Amazon/Kogan/direct-to-consumer brand websites in more digitally mature categories
BCF is exposed to weather/environmental disruption (algae bloom in SA, coastal disruption in Victoria) causing volatile like-for-like performance
Macpac's small scale (6% of Group sales) and high sensitivity to seasonal weather (mild winters depress demand) creates earnings volatility
Recent governance failure (CEO dismissal) exposed weaknesses in board oversight and executive accountability, with associated reputational and financial costs
Trade partners (branded suppliers) increasingly moving to direct-to-consumer models, a structural risk to rebel's model in particular

growth_drivers: New five-year strategy (launched June 2026) targeting mid-to-high single-digit annual normalised PBT growth through FY31, materially above prior consensus

Store network expansion from 797 to over 900 stores by 2031, with BCF targeting 190-200 stores (from 170) via large-format/superstore rollout, Supercheap Auto pursuing a new Generation 5 format, and rebel continuing its rCX format rollout

Ignite transformation program: ~$30m/year of project investment over three years (within the existing ~$150m p.a. capex envelope) targeting ~$75 million of annual cost savings by FY29 through digital, data, AI and a new ERP/systems foundation

Loyalty program monetization: 13.1 million active Club members, new Supercheap Auto 'Spend & Get' program (launched July 2025) and rebel Active program aimed at increasing visitation, spend and personalisation across the customer base
New Truganina, Victoria distribution centre (now servicing Supercheap Auto, rebel and BCF) to simplify product flows, improve inventory availability and support scale

Category tailwinds: rising vehicle fleet and SUV/4WD popularity (auto), growing participation in outdoor/hiking/camping and international tourism (Macpac, BCF), broad-based sporting/lifestyle demand (rebel)
Fitment and services expansion at Supercheap Auto (installation, diagnostics) to deepen customer engagement beyond pure product sales
Online and omni-channel investment continuing to grow Click & Collect penetration and fulfilment efficiency

business.description: All four banners sell largely discretionary goods; FY26 saw like-for-like momentum stall in H2 due to fuel price crisis, interest rates and cost-of-living pressures, and management flags continued uncertainty for FY27

Formally identified as a top strategic risk; increasing online/offline competition, aggressive competitor pricing, and the risk that trade partners shift to direct-to-consumer channels could erode market share across all banners

business.risk: Banner-level performance divergence and weather sensitivity
business.description: BCF (algae bloom, coastal disruption) and Macpac (mild winters) demonstrated in FY26 that leisure/outdoor categories are exposed to unpredictable weather and environmental events that can swing segment profit meaningfully year to year

business.risk: Execution risk on new strategy/Ignite program
business.description: The ambitious FY31 targets (mid-to-high single-digit PBT growth, 130+ new stores, $75m of cost savings) depend on successful, multi-year execution of a new ERP, AI and systems transformation under newly appointed leadership

financial.description: Normalised CODB rose 5.6% in FY26 (90bps as % of sales) due to network expansion, wage/occupancy inflation, and one-off transformation project costs (Truganina DC transition, new HR/payroll system)
A 13% AUD:NZD appreciation in FY26 created a translation headwind for Macpac's New Zealand-derived revenue and profit (constant-currency PBT growth of 44.7% vs reported 32.0%)

financial.risk: Reduced dividend payout / capital allocation shift
financial.description: FY26 aggregate dividends fell 32.3% YoY (to 65 cents/share) as the FY25 special dividend was not repeated and DRP remains suspended, reflecting a shift toward funding growth capex over shareholder returns

regulatory.risk: Employment law and workplace conduct compliance
regulatory.description: Complex employment instruments across Australia, New Zealand and China create wage remediation and compliance risk; the Group incurred wage remediation execution costs and separately faced litigation and reputational damage tied to workplace conduct/governance failures in FY25-26

FY26 normalised NPAT excluded $20.0m (after tax) of 'net legal and professional advisory fees and other adjustments related to regulatory and litigation matters', up from $7.9m in FY25, reflecting the costs of the CEO dismissal and related whistleblower litigation
Multi-category retailer subject to product recall, compliance and consumer protection regulation across three jurisdictions
Group published its inaugural climate-related financial disclosures in FY26 under new mandatory reporting regimes, adding compliance costs and disclosure risk

macro.description: Management explicitly cites rising interest rates and pressure on housing markets as weighing on near-term consumer confidence and discretionary spending

The FY26 result was materially affected by a domestic fuel price crisis linked to Middle East conflict/Strait of Hormuz tensions; management flags continued uncertainty into FY27 despite recent stabilisation

macro.risk: Freight, logistics and input cost inflation
macro.description: Elevated shipping/freight volatility, tariff changes and wage inflation continue to pressure cost of doing business across the network
Constrained labour markets in Australia/NZ contribute to wage growth pressure and retail crime-related staff turnover risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian/NZ specialty retail in auto, sport and outdoor categories is viewed by management as structurally under-penetrated (SUL captures only ~10% of a $65bn addressable market), but near-term conditions are challenging amid elevated interest rates, cost-of-living pressure and volatile fuel/energy prices
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - consumer discretionary spending categories that are sensitive to interest rates, fuel prices, weather and consumer confidence; loyalty programs and repeat-purchase categories (auto servicing/parts) provide some resilience relative to pure lifestyle/apparel retail
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - primarily indirect via consumer discretionary spending and mortgage-stressed household budgets rather than direct balance sheet exposure (Group carries minimal net debt, targeting 0-0.5x net debt/EBITDA pre-AASB16)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: AUD/NZD translation exposure via Macpac and New Zealand Supercheap Auto/other operations; a strengthening AUD versus NZD is a headwind to reported (though not constant-currency) earnings
key_input_costs: Cost of goods (import cost inflation, tariffs)
Fuel prices (indirect, via consumer demand for leisure/auto categories)

recent_developments.event: Board dismissed Group MD & CEO Anthony Heraghty with immediate effect over inadequate disclosure of a personal relationship with the former Chief HR Officer, following an 18-month whistleblower dispute alleging a toxic workplace; CFO David Burns appointed interim CEO; all Heraghty's unvested/unexercised incentives (~$3.3-3.4m) were forfeited; shares fell as much as 7% on the news

Whistleblower litigation brought by former Chief Legal Officer/Company Secretary and a General Manager alleging bullying, unreasonable workloads and suppression of information was settled confidentially in FY26, for less than the previously disclosed $30-50m estimated exposure range; FY26 accounts show $20.0m after-tax of related legal/professional advisory costs excluded from normalised NPAT
Paul Bradshaw (former BCF Managing Director, credited with 85% sales growth and near-tripling of BCF's PBT) appointed Group Managing Director and CEO following a global executive search
H1 FY26 result: revenue up 4.2% to $2,194.7m but statutory NPAT down 19.8% to $104.1m; interim dividend of 32.0 cps declared; DRP remained suspended

Investor Day: Group unveiled new five-year strategy targeting mid-to-high single-digit annual normalised PBT growth to FY31 (~7% above prior consensus), store network growth from 790 to 900+ stores, and the 'Ignite' transformation program targeting ~$75m of annual cost savings by FY29 via AI/data/ERP investment; analysts broadly positive (Jarden raised target to $15.60, Overweight; Macquarie called valuation 'compelling' at ~3x EV/EBITDA) though some remained cautious (Morgans Hold) on near-term consumer softness

FY26 results: record sales of $4.2bn (+3.2%) but normalised PBT down 7% to $306.2m and statutory NPAT down 7.2% to $205.9m on higher CODB and transformation project costs; gross margin improved 10bps to 45.7%; net debt of only $14m; final dividend of 33 cps (65 cps total for FY26, down 32.3% YoY due to non-repeat of FY25 special dividend); shares surged ~15.8% on the day as investors focused on FY27 trading momentum and cash generation over near-term earnings pressure

FY27 early trading update (first 7 weeks): Group like-for-like sales +1.5%, total sales +3.5%; Supercheap Auto +4.0% LFL (Best Performing Oils campaign); BCF +0.4% LFL with 5.5% total growth from new superstores; Macpac LFL down 8.9% on mild winter conditions
FY27 guidance: ~$160m capex (store development plus Project Ignite, majority technology/systems-based) and ~$60m Group/unallocated costs (~$30m ongoing corporate, ~$30m Ignite investment)

Executive leadership refresh: Ben McConnell (MD Supercheap Auto), Michael Wassman (MD BCF), Reuben Casey (MD Macpac), Jenny Child (MD rebel, from June 2026), Amy Bentley (Chief Supply Chain and Efficiency Officer), Sarah Hunter (incoming CFO) and Inga Kirkman (Chief Legal Officer & Company Secretary) all appointed as part of a broad management reset following the 2025 governance crisis

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Results / Appendix 4E, 20 August 2026 (plus June 2026 Investor Day strategy targets)

items.notes: Up from ~$150m FY26 envelope; majority technology/systems-based, funding store development plus Project Ignite
Reflects incremental Ignite transformation spend layered on top of ongoing corporate costs
First multi-year target under new five-year strategy launched June 2026; reported ~7% above prior consensus expectations at the time
Brand-level annual store growth targets: Supercheap Auto ~3%, rebel ~5%, BCF ~3% (170 to 190-200 stores), Macpac ~2%
Funded via ~$30m/year of project investment over three years, within the existing capex envelope; targets digital, data, AI and ERP-driven efficiency
Group ended FY26 with net debt of only $14m, comfortably within the targeted range
FY26 aggregate ordinary dividends of 65 cps represented a 65% payout ratio, at the top end of the targeted range

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Paul Bradshaw described FY26 as a 'difficult trading period' with a prolonged fuel crisis, unusual weather and household budget pressure, but noted FY27 trading has started with good momentum, particularly at Supercheap Auto and BCF, while Macpac faces headwinds from a mild winter. Management flagged that tensions in the Middle East remain elevated and create uncertainty for the FY27 outlook, alongside domestic pressures from interest rates, inflation and softer housing markets. The Board and executive team stated they are 'firmly aligned' on strategic priorities following the leadership transition and reiterated confidence in the new five-year strategy and Ignite program to deliver long-term shareholder value.

bull_case: New five-year strategy targets mid-to-high single-digit normalised PBT growth to FY31, well above prior market expectations, with a credible plan (store growth, format upgrades, Ignite transformation) now in place under fresh leadership

Extremely strong balance sheet (net debt of just $14m, 0-0.5x targeted gearing) and high cash conversion (92% operating cash conversion in FY26) provide substantial capacity to fund growth capex while sustaining a 55-65% dividend payout
13.1 million active loyalty members representing 86% of Group sales give the company a proprietary data asset and CRM capability that smaller independent competitors cannot easily replicate
Company estimates it captures only ~10% of a $65bn addressable market across auto, sport and outdoor categories in ANZ, implying substantial multi-year runway for organic store and category expansion

FY27 has started with encouraging early trading momentum (Group LFL +1.5%, Supercheap Auto +4.0% LFL) and shares re-rated sharply (+15.8%) on the FY26 result day as the market looked through near-term margin pressure to the growth plan and cash generation
bear_case: FY26 profitability declined materially (normalised PBT -7%, statutory NPAT -7.2%) even as sales grew, reflecting rising cost of doing business and heavy transformation project spend that may persist for several years before Ignite's promised $75m of savings materialise

2025 governance crisis (CEO dismissal over an undisclosed relationship, whistleblower litigation, ~$20m of after-tax legal/advisory costs in FY26 alone) exposed weaknesses in board oversight and executive accountability that could resurface or leave lingering reputational damage

Consumer discretionary spending remains under pressure from interest rates, cost-of-living and volatile fuel prices; management explicitly flags continued uncertainty for FY27, and BCF and Macpac results in FY26 show how weather and macro shocks can swing segment profits sharply

Execution risk is high: the new strategy relies on a largely refreshed executive team (new CEO, CFO, and multiple Managing Directors all appointed within the past 12-18 months) successfully delivering an ambitious multi-year store rollout and ERP/AI transformation simultaneously

Structural competitive threats persist, including trade partners moving to direct-to-consumer models, aggressive online/offline competitors (Amazon, Kogan, category specialists), and only modest online penetration (13% of sales) relative to more digitally advanced retail peers
